evidence:
Workbook quality row 17 asks whether the reference plausibly implements every requested feature/screen; frozen quality-checks.md:75-77 directs a brief-to-solution walk. No omitted capability was found. Paths below are relative to .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task unless marked otherwise.

Coverage: instruction.md:5/13/15 maps to public/js/app.js:21-28 (six workspaces), :232-266 (open requisitions, headroom, committed and pending dashboard figures), :79-84/:331-336 (signed-in name, role and approver tier), :114-123/:181-219/:316-329/:385-397 (loading/errors, form preservation, theme persistence and dialog keyboard support); public/index.html:10-26/46-50 supplies navigation/main landmarks, labelled login fields and modal semantics. public/js/hireops.js:61-89 and :203-260 implement requisition and offer entry, including user-supplied IDs and separate hire/referral dates. :121-168 shows all compensation inputs plus intrinsic/annualized equity, run-rate, band basis/tier, grants, signing history and rescission figures together. :45-58 shows live headroom and its movements; :175-197 supports six-field revision and dated rescission; :264-319 implements Equity Table and Referrals with grants, schedules, historical states, cancellations and the split referral bonus/cliff. :321-416 implements readable audit lines and expandable before/after receipts. CSS includes both themes, focus indicators, responsive cards, scrolling tables and mobile layouts. The inspected 390px dark-mode screenshot shows a usable Audit Trail with APPROVE, REVISE and RESCIND receipt cards.

Rules coverage: src/index.js:64-82/:88-109 resolves server sessions and demo identities; :197-226 protects operational reads; :229-249 validates preserved IDs, exact integers and dates; :289-323 implements allowed creation; :325-350 makes approval authority/dual-control/budget decisions and mints records atomically; :352-383 performs immutable predecessor revision, reversal/new commitment, signed payment adjustment and replacement grant; :385-408 settles only the current offer at the supplied effective date; :270-287 writes actor/before/after receipts in the same transaction; :411-420 refuses receipt/log mutations. src/rules.js:24-55/:62-99/:105-183 implements exact half-up composition, half-open bands, calendar anniversaries, distinct signing/equity vesting, referral cliff, live headroom and lineage signing totals. src/db.js:14-28/:122-180 supplies DB_PATH, colocated seed, SQLite persistence and seed-once behavior; src/bootstrap.js supplies independent health and one-process UI/API serving. The enumerated reference tree contains no shipped database.

Measured corroboration, checked against actual drivers and observations: local/domain/results.json records 77 passing HTTP observations, with 35 source-file hashes independently matching the frozen task; local/ui/results.json records 16 passing browser observations with all 12 source hashes matching the frozen solution. Raw domain/requests.json has 310 requests. The domain-offer-47 -> -R -> -R-R chain has successful approval, two revisions and rescission; the final raw response reports 480002 retained/net signing cents, 720003 clawback cents, 3 retained equity units and 10 cancelled units. Repeated/stale ancestor/current actions return 409. The driver verifies preserved old receipts, signed adjustments, role/tier controls with positive controls, competing approvals, calendar boundaries, referral dates, invalid-input rollback and unchanged business state after actual process replacement. UI observations cover arbitrary padded IDs, exact cents, visible complete compensation figures, dialog focus, retained invalid forms, revision/rescission and all six workspaces at 390px; its audit assertion alone is weak, so readable nested receipts are also verified in source and the screenshot. Installer evidence shows real unprivileged launch and MCP process replacement (PID 21 to 97) with saved-data readback. MCP results separately show a fresh browser context signing in and reading a UI-created requisition.

Hashes recomputed against raw-evidence-index.json: domain/results.json=96b7f34132e705013a7ef605d139de3ebac0274b508ca5f43cb5372584b841bd; domain/requests.json=9911838e598bc705facd45fa5bfbc82ea0d01c79b4bc8e927f2d4dbc18e5939b; ui/results.json=0b8cf0734fdd1f3bf5a503c997970550fd799bc88b869d03e95833d89b461ba7; ui/mobile-audit-dark.png=93147086535727fef8bdb8e63edf1cb2ae02071bd38b44c53294620b2daf531a; install-lifecycle/results.json=613da9cf8e275402f708957981b3cefe2236d55803f7b9efaaee7618e1ff15a8; mcp/results.json=c0a3672dfb069b54a930a07dd2b16a7582c097082cba544980666647da71513a. The domain and UI driver hashes also match their index entries.

Adversarial consideration: a static six-screen mock or a revision implementation that overwrites the previous grant could look complete but would not satisfy this review's checked transactional handlers, raw two-revision/settlement trace, preserved receipts and restart readback. A conforming alternative may use different routes, generated revision IDs, layout or a retained-grant representation; none is treated as an extra requirement here. This Pass is limited to plausible reference deliverable coverage. Scripted golden, MCP and installer observations are not a configured judge run, Oracle/model score or hosted clearance; none is claimed or needed to substitute for those separate audit rows.
